mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors interpret this as a sign of economic strength and potential increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS declined by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic output and corporate profits.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors interpret this as a sign of economic strength and increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and related sectors' growth.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure under a tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced purchasing power and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the described conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same quarter, it signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and UNRATE increases > 0.2pp in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the described conditions are met.
